summary.headline: Seojin System signs KRW 165.6bn SOFC fuel cell module supply deal with Bloom Energy
summary.what_happened: Seojin System Co., Ltd. disclosed a single supply contract to produce solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) modules and parts for Bloom Energy Corporation, a US counterparty, for a total contract amount of KRW 165.6bn, equal to USD 122,988,000 at the Seoul rate of 1,346.60 KRW/USD. The contract period runs from Nov 24, 2026 to Dec 19, 2027, with the order received on Nov 24, 2026, and production is outsourced to the company's overseas subsidiary in Vietnam.

key_numbers.label: Share of recent revenue (as stated in filing)
Payment terms
key_numbers.value: Payment within 45 days of invoice; EXW delivery from Vietnam plant; no advance payment

summary.why_it_matters: Large supply contracts disclosed under Korean exchange rules show the size of a company's order backlog and can indicate changes in its future revenue, though amounts, timing and terms may still be adjusted through later negotiations with the customer. Investors typically look at the contract size relative to the company's revenue and at whether the contract has conditions or payment risks.
